title: Tenant-aware ephemeral bloom + jump-indexing for sparse dashboard result sets
creator: Alex Kim
description: Deep offsets in dashboard queries (eg. Recent Activity / Events) for sparsely matching tenants cause large scan amplification and high tail latency. This ticket implements a coordinator-side, tenant-aware ephemeral bloom sketch plus jump-index pointer mechanism to skip non-matching index segments and accelerate paginated reads without changing the user-visible cursor semantics.
background: Observed during Q1 on multiple dashboards: tenants with large event stores and sparse matching filters (eg. rare event types, long time windows) see 95p latencies spike to 3–8s for pages beyond offset 2000. Existing approaches (larger page sizes, hedging) either increase cost or break UX. Previous tickets addressed cursor stability and prefetching but don't efficiently skip long empty index spans for sparse queries.
proposed_solution: When a dashboard query with filter X arrives, the query coordinator will construct an ephemeral per-tenant bloom sketch of anchor points sampled from inverted index segment summaries (lightweight per-shard summaries kept in the coordinator cache). The bloom indicates which segments likely contain matches. The coordinator uses a jump-index table of segment anchors (segment -> approximate first-match-offset) to jump over segments the bloom says are empty, issuing targeted segment fetches instead of scanning every shard in range. For safety, fall back to existing cursor scan when bloom uncertainty is high and validate correctness by cross-checking first item of each jumped segment.
data_model_changes: No persistent schema changes. We will maintain a small in-memory anchor table in the coordinator service and a per-tenant ephemeral bloom during query execution. Anchor metadata is derived from existing segment summaries; persisted summaries (compressed) already exist in the indexer service.
API_changes: No external API changes. Cursors remain opaque and stable. We add an internal query flag 'jump_index_v1' toggleable via feature flag. Admin/experiment metrics will expose whether jump-index was used on each request.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind ffkey=jump_index_v1. 2) Canary: enable for 5% of tenants (low variability tenants) for 48h. 3) Monitor correctness/latency/cost metrics. 4) Expand to 25% then 50% over 2 weeks if no regressions. 5) Full rollout after two post-canary incidents-free cycles and SRE sign-off. Rollback path: disable ffkey to revert to existing scanning behavior.
testing_plan: Unit tests for bloom creation and false-positive bounds. Integration test harness simulating sparse and dense tenants with mixed writes while paginating. Property tests ensuring no result-loss and cursor monotonicity. Load test in staging with realistic shard counts and query mixes. Add golden queries to end-to-end CI comparing outputs between jump-index enabled and disabled.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: No missing or duplicated results across paginated sequences for 99.999% of synthetic queries (allowable 1e-5 false-positive recheck rate).
Perf: For sparse-query tenant cohort, 95th percentile page latency for offsets >2000 reduced by >=60% compared to baseline.
Cost: Coordinator CPU increase <=15% and overall byte-read from storage for sampled sparse queries reduced by >=40%.
Reliability: Error rate (5xx) introduced by change < 0.01% and < baseline + 0.01%
Operational: Feature flag toggle works and rollback within 2 minutes without client impact.
implementation_notes:
- Build 'anchor sampler' that runs at segment-rollup time to emit segment anchor fingerprints.
- Use an optimized golang bloom implementation tuned for small number of anchors (~256 anchors typical).
- Add jump-index lookup layer inside coordinator's QueryPlanner; planner will annotate fetch plan with 'jump' ranges.
- Ensure concurrency safety: ephemeral bloom only lives for the request and is GC'd.
- Validate with a deterministic recheck of first N results from any jumped segment to ensure correctness in the presence of racey writes. Recheck cost accounted in perf budget.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Dashboards: 'jump_index_usage', 'jump_index_false_rechecks', 'jump_index_95p_latency', 'jump_index_coord_cpu'
- Alerts: paging_latency_95p_increase > 10% vs baseline for 15m; false_recheck_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m; coordinator_cpu_delta > 30% sustained.
perf_targets: 95p latency for deep pages (>2000 offset) should be < 600ms for sparse cohort; median should improve proportionally. Coordinated I/O reduction goal: >40% for sampled queries.
